handled_verified._description: Analyzer-referenced node types; behavior probe-verified 2026-09-18 against the pinned wasm via real-elixir-analyzer.ts. Every type below was observed in a hasError=false live parse and its emission path confirmed (symbols/relationships/complexity) through the analyzer. quoted_keyword closed fixture-first the same day (ELXD5: defstruct ["a": 1] now emits the field; fixture quoted-struct-fields + mutant elixir/drop-quoted-struct-fields).

internal_silent._description: Grammar-internal containers, literals, comments, and structural wrappers that correctly emit nothing (no relationship semantics in the analyzer's contract). Each verified with a hasError=false live parse 2026-09-18 showing the wrapper contributes no symbol, edge, or complexity delta (e.g. parenblock vs plainarith identical; strlit/strinterp/stresc/sigilplain/sigilmod/charlit/charlistlit/bitstring/tuplelit/boollit/nillit/quotedatom/commentonly/floata/access probes).

gap._description: Confirmed missing emissions the analyzer does not model (declared limitations, each a tracked work item). EX-G1 (quoted_keyword struct fields) closed fixture-first 2026-09-18 as ELXD5. The original 'no open gaps' claim was falsified at EX-F5 certification (2026-09-19): the F5 corpus differential found the Registry.Supervisor implied-alias non-edge — EX-L5 registered the last-segment alias at module ENTRY, so `use Supervisor` inside Registry.Supervisor self-resolved and was dropped; the fix moves registration to module EXIT (fixture implied-alias-scope + mutant elixir/implied-alias-entry-time) and both corpora re-measure 100%/0/0. The claim was falsified AGAIN by the independent adversarial review (EX-ADV, 2026-09-19): 13 defect classes, every one on the gate's blind side (mirrored rules, last-segment masking, gate-invisible labels) — fixed and pinned; full record in reviews/elixir/adversarial-2026-09-19.md. The gap list resumes empty WITH both falsifications on record; the census classification (2026-09-18) predates EX2/EX3/EX-F5/EX-ADV — re-classification is registered, not silent. A THIRD falsification arrived on 2026-09-28, and it came from the only instrument that is not a mirror: the oracle-blind deep audit (`script/m14/tmp/elixir-deep-audit.ts`), which checks containment, identity and range arithmetic instead of re-deriving the rules. It found three defect classes on a lane every other gate called clean — the merged-head extent (EX-D16), the `raise` construction (EX-D17) and the nested-module owner (EX-D18) — plus a spec-side measurement: 116 distinct node types over 697 files of six corpora, ZERO named types unclassified (`script/m14/tmp/elixir-spec-census.ts`), one classified type (`charlist`) with no live site in that sample. The lesson is the one the adversarial wave already paid for: a differential against a second implementation of the same rules certifies CONSISTENCY, and this lane's newest classes were all invisible to it. A FOURTH falsification, 2026-09-28, from a second oracle-blind instrument built for exactly this question: the per-DECLARATION-FORM coverage census (`script/m14/tmp/elixir-declaration-census.ts`). Classifying node types was the wrong granularity — a node type can be 'handled' while the DECLARATION it carries publishes nothing, and that is precisely what `@callback` was: 165 sites, 0 covered, on a lane every other gate called clean. EX-D21 closes it; EX-D22 records what the census does and does not prove.

design_decision.description: Elixir analyzer contract (ELXD waves, probe-verified 2026-09-18): quote-as-data, Kernel-builtin exclusion, member-access exclusion, def-head/attribute exclusion, struct-literal gating, pipe/unqualified-call resolution.

decisions.question: Code inside `quote do ... end` is macro AST data, not executable module code.
decisions.resolution: RULED: everything under a quote-headed call is skipped — no symbols, no call edges, no directives (isInQuotedCode; quotedblock probe emits nothing inside quote). AMENDED (adversarial X1, 2026-09-19): the `@`-attribute branch had run UNGUARDED inside quote blocks — `@behaviour`/`@type` in quoted code emitted implements edges (including garbage `unquote(behaviour)` targets) and Type symbols; live instances existed in elixir's own Application.__using__ and Protocol.__impl__/__derive__. The guard now covers it. AMENDED AGAIN (X7): `unquote`/`unquote_splicing` ARGUMENTS execute at expansion time — the nearest unquote boundary wins over the enclosing quote and their calls walk (26+7 corpus sites).

decisions.question: Kernel builtins (length, hd, is_atom, inspect, self, spawn, send, struct, ...) are available in every module — do they produce calls edges?
decisions.resolution: RULED: following the FP-family precedent (Clojure core builtins), KERNEL_FUNCTIONS are excluded from calls edges — they add pure noise to the call graph (real-elixir-analyzer.ts:66). spawn/send still mark Actor Model patterns. AMENDED (adversarial X9): the exclusion extends to `Kernel.`-QUALIFIED spellings — 49 corpus sites emitted `Kernel.length`/`Kernel.raise` while bare ones were silent. AMENDED (capture companion): only UNQUALIFIED captures consult the Kernel set — `&String.length/1` is a remote reference whose leaf merely collides; the leaf-keyed check silently dropped String.length/IO.inspect/List.to_string captures once the generic re-emission of the capture head was suppressed.

decisions.question: Member/property access `order.side` parses as a call with a dot target and no arguments — invocation or field read?
decisions.resolution: RULED: argument-less dot-target calls are field reads and emit no edge; module calls like Map.put(...) carry arguments and are real invocations (isMemberAccess, verified memberaccess vs dotcall probes 2026-09-18).

decisions.question: Declaration-head calls (def signatures, defstruct macro heads, @attribute inner calls) look like invocations.
decisions.resolution: RULED: signature calls nested in def arguments, calls inside @attributes, and defmacro defstruct heads never emit — they are declarations, not call sites (isDefHead/isInAttribute; ELXD4 kernel.ex:5624 phantom fix; attrtype/attrbeh probes emit Type/implements, never calls).

decisions.question: Which %{} literals are struct instantiations?
decisions.resolution: RULED: only alias-backed struct literals (%StructName{...}, not %{} or %__MODULE__{}) in executable position (never a def signature, attribute, or quoted block) emit instantiates (structlit probe emits instantiates f->Foo; isInDefHeadOrAttribute). AMENDED (adversarial X2): PATTERN positions are never constructions either — case/fn/receive clause patterns (stab_clause before the anonymous `->` token) and the left of `=`/`<-` are destructures; 43+16 live corpus sites fabricated an instantiates each.

decisions.question: Pipe chains and unqualified local calls: what resolves to an edge?
decisions.resolution: RULED: `|>` RHS emits a calls edge with isPipe metadata (pipe probe); unqualified calls inside a module resolve post-walk against the enclosing module's declared set so forward references work, and names matching nothing declared resolve through :only-constrained imports (last import wins — ELXD17) or are dropped, never fabricated (bare/:except imports cannot confirm a target); Kernel auto-imports (full surface per ELXD16) never emit; at top level (script files, no enclosing module) unqualified calls are KEPT — there is no scope to resolve against, so dropping would lose real edges (test/describe/setup DSL included). Erlang `:mod.fun()` calls emit with source-faithful atom-root targets. (declaredByScope filter + resolveImport, real-elixir-analyzer.ts:270).

decisions.question: Elixir dispatches on name+arity (foo/1 and foo/2 are different functions) — do call edges carry arity?
decisions.resolution: RULED arity-blind, family-wide standard: calls resolve and emit by name only (heads/arity stay on the symbol metadata). Arity-qualifying every edge would rebuild the family's call model for one language; the loss is disambiguation between same-name arities, never missing edges.

decisions.question: `use` macros inject definitions (`__using__`/`__before_compile__` — e.g. GenServer's child_spec/1) that never appear as syntax — are injected functions modeled?
decisions.resolution: RULED macro-expansion boundary (C-D2 class): only syntactically present declarations become symbols; injected definitions are invisible, so qualified calls to them stay dropped as undeclared. Modeling them would require expanding every macro — statically unbounded. `use` still emits its references edge and OTP behavior marking.

decisions.question: Dynamically-named definitions (`def unquote(name)()`, `defmacro ^var`, `defguard("literal is bad")` in error tests) cannot be named statically — placeholder or drop?
decisions.resolution: RULED: they keep a visible `Unknown` placeholder symbol (25 sites across both corpora, every one verified unquote/pin/degenerate-string headed — never a missed static name after ELXD23/ELXD24). No call site can name them, so they never match resolution; dropping them would lose the definition's existence.

decisions.question: EXL-5: the `case` construct (+1) AND each clause (+1) both count, one higher than kotlin/java/TS per-entry granularity (switch_case/when_entry only, +1 each). Align or declare?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-19): keep and DECLARE. The lane counts the conditional construct itself for every conditional macro (`if`/`unless`/`case`/`cond`/`receive`/`with`) so construct-only forms (`cond`, `with` — no separate clause nodes) are not undercounted against their `if`-chain equivalents; `case` additionally counts its `stab_clause` branches. Net divergence: +1 per `case` construct vs the JVM/TS per-entry convention — recorded here, pinned by the `complexity-forms` module=3 fixture, and registered for the CC1 cross-language-consistency audit rather than changed unilaterally (defs-as-decision is likewise fixture-pinned).

decisions.question: X7: `unquote`/`unquote_splicing` arguments are they data (inside the quote skip) or code?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial X7): CODE — they execute during macro expansion. The nearest unquote boundary wins over the enclosing quote; the rest of the quote block stays data. Unquoted calls then obey the normal call rules (including the declared ELXD17 resolution policy for unqualified names). Fixture unquote-code + mutant elixir/unquote-dropped.

decisions.question: X6: what arity do pipe steps carry?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial X6): THREAD-ADJUSTED — the piped value is an argument: written args + 1 (`x |> f(1)` is f/2); a bare `x |> g` carries arity 1; the step's own walk never re-emits the written arity. Fixture pipe-arity + mutant elixir/pipe-arity-raw.

decisions.question: X8: does defdelegate emit a link to its delegated target?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial X8): YES — a calls edge from the delegate to `<to:>.<name>` (to: alias-resolved; `as:` renames the segment), line = the to: value; 71+12 corpus definitions carried zero dependency signal. Fixture defdelegate + mutant elixir/defdelegate-dropped.

decisions.question: X4/X5: chained-receiver targets and `__MODULE__.fun` — what identity do they carry?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial X4/X5): a call whose receiver is a call result (`Mix.shell().error`) targets the METHOD LEAF (`error`) and skips declared-set resolution — never call syntax in an identity (148+91 corpus edges). `__MODULE__.fun` resolves to the nearest module scope (ELXD21 parity; 5+8 sites), dropped when no module encloses. Fixtures chained-calls/module-self-call + mutants elixir/chained-target-kept, elixir/module-literal-target.

decisions.question: X13/X12: do arity-distinct same-line sites both survive, and which line do multi-line alias members carry?
decisions.resolution: RULED (adversarial): callArity joins the dedupe identity key — `{f(1), f(2, 3)}` keeps both edges (EX-L2's name+arity contract, completed); and each member of a multi-line alias list carries its OWN name-bearing line. Fixtures same-line-arity/alias-members-lines + mutants elixir/same-line-arity-collapse, elixir/alias-member-line.

decisions.question: EX-A8: a MERGED multi-clause definition (one `def f/1` symbol, `heads: N`) carried only its FIRST clause's range, so the payload claimed seven clauses and located one. What is a merged definition's extent?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): first clause start .. LAST CLAUSE end, with the start (the declaration site every id and name-line consumer is built on) untouched — the rule real-clean-analyzer.ts already applies to a multi-clause `f x = ...`. The exact per-clause ranges ride `metadata.clauseRanges`, because the span alone cannot recover them: measured on elixir@024beb1b, 195 of 2,321 merged groups (8.4%) carry OTHER declarations between their first and last clause (`Date.to_string/1` spans 335..1170 and swallows 54 defs). Measured before the fix: 184 clause-span violations in a 60-file ecto_sql slice (`def loaders/2` heads=7, range 211..211). Fixture merged-clause-extent pins range endLine/endColumn/endIndex + meta.clauseRanges; mutants elixir/merged-head-range-first-clause and elixir/merged-head-clause-ranges-dropped CAUGHT. Finding instrument: script/m14/tmp/elixir-deep-audit.ts (A8, measured off the TREE, not off the analyzer's own merge bookkeeping).

decisions.question: EX-A9: `raise Mod` / `raise Mod, msg` / `reraise Mod, stack` is `Mod.exception([])`, which BUILDS `%Mod{}` — the same construction the lane already emits an `instantiates` edge for at `struct(User, attrs)` (ELXD19) and a `%Mod{}` literal. It emitted nothing, because `raise` is a special form.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): `raise`/`reraise` emit an instantiates edge to a statically NAMED first argument (an `alias`, alias-resolved, or `__MODULE__`) and never a call (both stay in SPECIAL_FORMS). A bare `raise "msg"`, a bound exception, or a computed module name no type and stays silent — unnameable, not dropped. Measured: 401 alias-named raise sites in 200 files of elixir@024beb1b carried no dependency edge, while the defexception struct symbols they construct already existed. Fixture merged-clause-extent pins both directions; mutant elixir/raise-no-instantiates CAUGHT; oracle mirror landed in the same commit (deriveElixirEdges).

decisions.question: EX-A10: what is the `ownerName` of a module NESTED inside another module? The lane's own symbol contract says 'nested modules owned by the parent' and the M14 ledger ruling (#867) says `ownerName` is the innermost enclosing declaration — but the code wrote only `scope`.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): the enclosing declaration, exactly like every function/struct/field in the same file. Measured: 100% of nested-module symbols on the 60-file ecto_sql slice had ownerName undefined, and only the indexer's `ownerName || scope` fallback kept the graph right — the CONTRACT did not, and any consumer reading ownerName alone (src/ast/override-context.ts, src/ast/framework-intelligence.ts both do) saw a parentless module. The export surface is unaffected: a module is a public entry point whatever its nesting, so the export rule is now module-kind aware rather than owner-absence driven. Fixture merged-clause-extent + implied-alias-scope pin ownerName; mutant elixir/nested-module-ownerless CAUGHT.

decisions.question: EX-A13: the `isMessagePass`/`isSend` edge markers were built for `send`/`send_after`, but those are Kernel auto-imports, so EX-D2 drops them before any edge exists. Was the marker live?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): DEAD, and measured rather than assumed — a probe with `send(pid, :hi)` emits ZERO relationships, while the QUALIFIED spawn forms (`Task.async/1`, `Agent.start_link/1`, ...), which are ordinary module calls, do emit `isProcessSpawn`. The dead store is deleted rather than left to read as a payload; message passing survives as the file-level `Message Passing` idiom flag, and the reachable `isProcessSpawn` marker is pinned (fixture otp-messaging, new in this wave). A dead store that looks like a payload is the X11/EX-ADV prototype class in a new dress.

decisions.question: EX-A12: the single-argument `defimpl P do` form recorded `forType: "Unknown"` — a placeholder literal, the same literal this lane forbids as a SYMBOL name — while the implementation's own name held the real answer (the enclosing module).
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): `forType` records the type the implementation is for, resolved: the `for:` keyword's alias, the multi-type list, or the enclosing module for the single-argument form. When no type is derivable at all the field is ABSENT — absence is what 'unknown' is allowed to look like in a payload. Pinned by meta.forType in defimpl-target-forms and protocol-forms; mutant elixir/defimpl-fortype-dropped CAUGHT.

decisions.question: EX-A14: `@callback name(args) :: type` is a DECLARATION of a function — the same class of published fact as `@type` (which emits a Type symbol) — and it emitted a file-level `Behaviours` pattern flag and nothing else. Measured 165 sites in a 100-file elixir+phoenix+ash sample and 98 in a 171-file ecto+ecto_sql+wallaby sample, 0 covered. A module may declare a behaviour surface with no `def` at all, so the callback existed nowhere in the index.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): (1) a callback is a DECLARATION symbol — `isDeclaration: true` at the TOP level (the field the indexer binds to brain_symbol.is_declaration, #612, and the one the C and Clean lanes set for prototypes), kind Method inside a protocol/impl and Function elsewhere, carrying `callbackSpec` (the spec text) and `isCallback`/`isMacroCallback`; (2) identity is SHARED with the function merge key `owner.name/arity`, so `@callback load(t)` + `def load(x)` is ONE symbol carrying the spec, never two symbols for one function; (3) a clause WITH a body makes the merged symbol a DEFINITION and the declaration flag is REMOVED — a flag that survives a body would be a false statement the store persists; (4) `heads` counts clauses, so a callback (0 clauses) and a bodiless protocol head are not counted as heads; (5) a bodiless `def` is a declaration, detected structurally — no `do_block` and no `do:` pair inside the def's `arguments` (the pair is NESTED there, not a sibling: reading it as a sibling marked every `def f(x), do: y` a declaration); (6) `@optional_callbacks` ANNOTATES rather than declares — the names ride the owning protocol/module's `metadata.optionalCallbacks` and stamp the members, in both the bare-keyword and the LIST form (ash uses the list; the bare-only first version annotated nothing there); (7) the `::` operator is found by a depth-bounded search through binary operators, because a `when` constraint WRAPS the `::` expression (`@callback pop(d, k) :: {…} when d: container`) and the first version picked the wrong operator and published nothing. Fixture callback-declarations pins all seven; mutants elixir/callback-symbol-dropped, elixir/callback-duplicate-symbol, elixir/every-def-a-declaration, elixir/callback-spec-dropped CAUGHT. Finding instrument: script/m14/tmp/elixir-declaration-census.ts (per DECLARATION FORM, not per node type).

decisions.question: After EX-D21, what is the lane's output-coverage claim, and what does the census NOT prove?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): the claim is a per-FORM table, not a per-node-type list. Measured 2026-09-28 over 294 files (elixir+phoenix+ash, 100 each) and 171 files (ecto_sql+ecto+wallaby, 60 each): every live declaration form is 100% covered — defmodule 554/554, def 1689/1689, defp 1728/1728, defmacro 211/211, defimpl 32/32, defstruct 42/42, defexception 12/12, defdelegate 19/19, defprotocol 6/6, defguard 4/4, type 235/235, @callback 83/83, @optional_callbacks 5/5, @behaviour 15/15, @derive 3/3 (+1 dynamic, silent by contract), use 318/318, import 129/129, alias 121/121, require 22/22, @doc 951/951, @moduledoc 257/257, raise 255/255, struct 33/33. NOT claimed: that the F5 differential's silence arm is re-verified per form (it is verified once, bidirectionally, by the lane differential on six corpora); that a form with no live site in the sample is covered (before_compile/defoverridable/typedoc are reported as '(no live site)', never as OK); and the census's own artifacts are recorded rather than hidden — six of them, each adjudicated in reviews/elixir/deep-review-2026-09-28.md.

decisions.question: EX-A15: `defmacro (..) do … end` — a PARENTHESIZED operator definition with no argument list, which is how Kernel defines its zero-arity range operator (elixir/lib/elixir/lib/kernel.ex:4347). The grammar shapes the name as `arguments > block > operator_identifier`, which no signature branch recognised, so it fell through to the EX-D9 placeholder. Found by re-measuring EX-D9's claim: 20 `Unknown` symbols over 559 files / 10,745 symbols, 19 genuinely dynamic and exactly ONE a missed static name.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): the operator token is statically nameable, so the definition is named (`..`, `---`, `++`, …) and a second parenthesized operator no longer MERGES into the same placeholder row — pre-fix, two of them in one module produced ONE `Unknown` symbol (fixture paren-operator-forms measures `expected 1 symbol(s) named Unknown; got 2`). Arity comes from the sibling `arguments` node when the form carries one (`def (op)(a, b)` is an ERROR node in this grammar but its argument list is readable) and is 1 otherwise (the macro receives the single AST argument). The genuinely dynamic name keeps the placeholder, pinned positively (count = 1, kind, owner) because an expectation cannot assert a field's ABSENCE and the FORBID half pins the kind instead. Fixture paren-operator-forms (FAIL proved pre-fix) + mutant elixir/paren-operator-placeholder CAUGHT.

decisions.question: EX-A16: EX-D21 sets `isDeclaration: true` on a callback symbol, as the UniversalSymbol field the indexer's insert reads. Does that fact REACH brain_symbol.is_declaration?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-28): NO, not until the flag also rode `metadata.isDeclaration` — the ONE key the pool worker carries to the store phase (src/ast/pool-worker.ts, the #612 seam comment: the worker reconstructs the symbol field-by-field and carries one metadata key). Measured on a real index through `indexProjectParallel`: `brain_symbol.is_declaration` held 0 rows for elixir before the fix and 2 after (the callback declaration and the bodiless protocol head). The analyzer now publishes BOTH forms, the way the C analyzer publishes the metadata one, and the declaration-callbacks fixture pins the metadata key. This defect class is invisible to every analyzer-level gate by construction — fixtures call the analyzer and never pass through the worker — so the lane's SEAM gate is now `script/m14/tmp/elixir-store-roundtrip.ts`: a real Elixir app indexed by the production indexer and read back in SQL (symbols, owners, docstrings, scope_kind, is_declaration, the multi-clause extent, relationship source resolution, line_number, id-key collisions). Mutant elixir/declaration-metadata-key-dropped covers the payload half; the SQL probe covers the seam half.

decisions.question: EX-A17 (Master Review, 2026-09-29): every extraction site is gated by `isInAttribute`, on the stated ground that "the attribute's inner call is the attribute declaration, never a runtime invocation". That is true of the attribute's NAME and false of its VALUE: `@section %Spark.Dsl.Section{build: Spark.Dsl.build(:x)}` builds that struct while the module compiles, `@deferred fn -> Helper.later() end` names a real remote call, `@raised raise Helper.Error` raises a real exception, and the whole DSL ecosystem (Ash/Spark, Ecto.Migration, Quantum) is built on it. Measured 21 attributes carrying 21 struct literals in a 250-file sample of ash, 0 in 938 files of the other five corpora; 0 qualified calls in those attributes. The same walk ALREADY counted a `case` inside an attribute toward cyclomatic complexity and set its idiom flags, so the gate contradicted the analyzer's own treatment of one subtree.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): an attribute's VALUE is compile-time CODE, and its edges emit like any other code — `calls` and `instantiates` (including `raise`/`reraise`/`struct`) from a code-valued attribute. Two carve-outs, both load-bearing: (1) the attribute's OWN call node is its name (`@section` is call[section, arguments[…]]), so relaxing the gate for the value would otherwise publish a lowercase phantom call — `isAttributeNameCall` keeps that silent, and mutant elixir/attribute-name-call-fabricated pins it; (2) the DECLARATION attributes keep their silence: `doc`/`moduledoc` are text, `spec`/`type`/`typep`/`opaque`/`callback`/`macrocallback` are typespecs whose `%Mod{}` is a TYPE REFERENCE and not a construction (27 such sites in a 60-file elixir sample, 30 in ecto), `behaviour`/`behavior`/`derive`/`optional_callbacks` are contracts already published as `implements`, and `deprecated` is a string. `isInAttribute` still gates the directive and member-read walks, because a `use`/`alias` cannot legitimately appear in an attribute value. Fixture attribute-value-code (FAIL proved pre-fix, 10 missing edges) + mutants elixir/attribute-value-silenced and elixir/attribute-name-call-fabricated CAUGHT; F5 oracle mirror in deriveElixirEdges (isAttrNameCall/isDeclAttrValue) so both sides read the same rule — without the mirror the oracle would have ratified the silence as truth and the 21 ash sites would have read as 'no dependency' on BOTH sides, which is a shared blind spot, not agreement.

decisions.question: EX-A18 (Master Review, 2026-09-29): the multi-alias expander accepted only `alias` and `dot` members, so `alias Helper.{make, name}` — lowercase FUNCTION aliases, whose member node is an `identifier` — produced ZERO dependency edges and registered no local alias. The uppercase form (`alias Ecto.{Query, Repo}`) was already covered by ELXD20, which is why the hole survived: 38 uppercase members in a 60-file ecto_sql sample against 0 lowercase ones.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): members may be `alias`, `dot` or `identifier`, and the expansion registers the local name exactly as it does for the capitalized members. A bare call through a lowercase function alias is then statically nameable and resolves: `make()` becomes `calls -> Helper.make`. The resolution cannot capture anything else, because the alias map's only lowercase keys are the ones this form writes (module aliases and the implied `Task.Supervisor` -> Supervisor keys are capitalized). Corpus weight: 0 sites in 938 files of the six corpora — a LATENT hole, not a corpus defect, and recorded as such; it is fixed because the hole is one predicate wide and the rule is the one the uppercase members already follow. Fixture attribute-value-code + mutants elixir/multialias-lowercase-dropped and elixir/lowercase-alias-call-unresolved CAUGHT.

decisions.question: After EX-D25/EX-D26, what does 'every relationship is covered' mean, measured how, and what does the instrument itself get wrong?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): two claims, each with its own instrument, both run per corpus on a fixed 60-file sample. CLAIM 1 (line contract, M60): 0 line-less edges and every `contains` edge's line equals the member's own declaration line, checked EXACTLY per label (a call names its callee's line, a directive names the target node's line, an `instantiates` names the struct/exception's first argument) — no window, after the ±2-line heuristic of the earlier deep audit was replaced. CLAIM 2 (per-site identity): every naming construct in the file produced the edge it names — use/import/alias/require, %Mod{}, raise/reraise, struct/struct!, @behaviour, @derive, defimpl, Mod.fun(). Measured 2026-09-29 over 360 files of six corpora: 2,290/2,290 (100.00%), with the DECLARED silences counted and reported rather than assumed — 1,466 struct literals in pattern position (EX-D5/X2), 57 naming constructs inside a declaration attribute value (EX-D25) and self-directives (ELXD8). The instrument's own defects are part of the record, because an audit that cannot name a rule reports its own ignorance as analyzer loss: (1) it did not implement the pattern rule and reported 167 phantom missing `instantiates` in a 60-file slice, every one a def-head pattern; (2) its def-head half then compared web-tree-sitter node wrappers by IDENTITY (`.parent` returns a fresh wrapper per access), so the walk ran past the def into its do_block and returned false — 43 more phantoms; (3) its `=` rule returned its answer either way, so a default-bound struct in a signature (`insert_all(query = %Ecto.Query{}, _counter)`) looked like code; (4) it collected module spans from a direct `alias` child of the defmodule call when the name sits in its `arguments`, so the ELXD8 self-alias check could never fire. All four are fixed in the instrument, and CLAIM 2 stands at 100% only after they were — a number produced by a broken falsifier is not evidence. NOT claimed: that the six corpora are the whole of Elixir; that a name is extractable where the grammar yields none (the 21 `Unknown` placeholders over 1,586 files are all genuinely dynamic — `defmacro unquote(verb)(…)` names nothing static); that F5's per-file `catch { continue }` is safe (R4); or that the residual list R1-R7/R30 is closed.
